category_title: High-intensity students who rush through tasks and experience math anxiety
minimal_context: The student and tutor are working after school on a math assignment that requires calculating with decimals.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We need to work on calculating with decimals today. Let's set up this division problem.

STUDENT: I already wrote it down! I want to finish my homework in record time so I can go play sports.

TUTOR: Let's look at the steps. I will tell you which number goes in the division house.

STUDENT: (Moving with definite inner intensity) I'm just going to divide it this way so I can be done fast.

TUTOR: No, you need to follow the procedure. Put the other number inside.

STUDENT: That is not what my teacher told me! I hate this, math is like a scary movie!

options.A: Create open-ended problem-solving activities that require the student to use math concepts to construct something based on their personal preferences and interests.
options.B: Maintain a quiet and relaxing environment during the math session; talk gently and slowly to the student, and consistently avoid any loud speech.
options.C: Maintain a consistent ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 throughout the duration of the after-school math tutoring session.
options.D: Ensure that the student understands the vocabulary associated with division problems, such as 'in each' and 'distributed equally', then focus on filling in the model diagram.
